title: Evaluation report · run of 16 November 2026
headline: The assistant finds the right law and never misses dangerously; where it falls short it puts the right finding one severity step too high or too low.
summary: Routing, screens and the output guardrail are clean. Retrieval meets its target and the agentic loop finds three queries a single search misses. Quick answers cite the right article in 12 of 14 and stay within three sentences; one of the 15 questions was routed to the full path. All 20 feature descriptions reached the DPO's pause with an assessment, with no dangerous miss and every expected citation present; the high-risk AI flag was never missed and raised once without cause. Where the assistant falls short, it is on the severity of findings it has otherwise got right.

gateway_cost.note: OpenRouter activity page: 27 Oct for E1 E2 E7 E5 E6, 3 Nov for the E3 E4 re-run; the harness prices tokens only, the embeddings are the difference. A first E5 run on the shared retrieval set ($0.32) was superseded by the run on E5's own set; the E3 E4 run of 27 Oct ($0.10, with the Cohere reranker) by the re-run of 3 Nov.

failure_modes.title: Severity one step off
failure_modes.text: All five wrong verdicts are one step from the expected one, never two and never in the dangerous direction; 10 of the 17 missed findings make the right point with the right provision and only the wrong label. Four of them mark a point Required that the design or the organisation already covers, three raise a Required point to a Blocker and three lower a Blocker to Required.
failure_modes.example: A-001, a recently-viewed strip inside the customer's own account, expected Proceed: "Required: confirm the notice available when views are collected explains this specific account-only display … The existing general statement about browsing activity may not cover all required details (GDPR Art. 13(1), 13(2))".
failure_modes.response: Acceptable: the DPO can move a finding one step at the pause, and no verdict was two steps off or in the dangerous direction.

failure_modes.title: Special-category data as a Blocker where a consent route exists
failure_modes.text: Selfie verification with a video-call alternative (A-012) and a doctor's note for a payment holiday (A-017) expected a Required Art. 9(2)(a) finding and got a Blocker: the assistant treats a consent the description does not yet establish as a design fault rather than a condition. In A-017 this also moved the verdict to Do not build. A reasonable DPO could read it either way; these rows go to the human expert.
failure_modes.example: A-012, finding 1: "Blocker: do not build this path unless an Article 9(2) exception is established; if relying on explicit consent, it must be genuinely voluntary, with video-call verification a real alternative (GDPR Art. 9(1), 9(2))".
failure_modes.response: Resolved by the human in the loop: the DPO decides whether the consent route exists and lowers the finding to Required.

failure_modes.title: A DPIA left to the next steps
failure_modes.text: Profiling from card transactions for offers (A-007) and a vendor keeping transaction data for its own models (A-009) expected a DPIA before processing. Both assessments mention the DPIA only as something to check in the next steps and set the DPIA flag to no. These are the two missed DPIA flags.
failure_modes.example: A-009, next steps: "assess GDPR DPIA need if processing is likely to create high risk"; DPIA flag: no.
failure_modes.response: Caught by the DPO, who sets the flag at the pause. Both expectations are among those the human expert still reviews.

failure_modes.title: The point made outside the findings, or with the umbrella article
failure_modes.text: Seven of the nine partial findings are of two kinds. Four state the high-risk classification, or that the system is not high-risk, only in the summary or the flag, without a finding that cites Annex III. Three cite "GDPR Art. 5" for minimisation or storage limitation where 5(1)(c) or 5(1)(e) was expected. The worker's rule "cite the most specific label the tools returned" did not reach these.
failure_modes.example: A-017, findings 4 and 5: minimum proof and retention, both cited as "GDPR Art. 5".
failure_modes.response: Harmless to the DPO, who sees the point and the article; it costs the partial score only.

failure_modes.title: AI Act Art. 5 is the corpus's weak spot
failure_modes.text: Missed by the single pass in E3 twice, by the loop once, and by the E5 question that needed it: the article's chunks are long and the recitals that paraphrase it (Rec. 30, Rec. 31) outrank it. A corpus-side fix (shorter chunks, a heading that names the practices) belongs to the embedding and chunking study after the capstone.
failure_modes.example: K-008, social scoring: answered from Rec. 31, without the Art. 5 chunk.
failure_modes.response: A corpus fix: shorter chunks for Art. 5 with a heading that names the practices, so the article outranks the recitals that paraphrase it.

judge_note: The judge was checked against a blind human reading on the run of 27 October, not on this one. There, the target was written as 17 of 20 on the assumption of 20 scorable rows; with 4 unsure rows left out, 13 of 15 is 0.87 against 0.85. In both disagreements the judge was the more generous reader, and it was strict in one systematic way, counting a point made only in the summary as absent. The unsure rows and the disagreements go to the human expert in round 3.
limitations: One run per case, 20 cases, 15 questions: the numbers locate failure modes, they do not give confidence intervals. The two assessment runs of 16 November, which differ in one prompt rule, gave 16 and 15 right verdicts and 58 and 55 matched findings.

The test data was reviewed by an AI model acting as the domain expert (two rounds); the human expert's review is pending, and the DPIA (A-007, A-009) and Art. 9 severity (A-012, A-017) expectations are the ones most likely to move.
The reviser (E9) and the memory's effect on later assessments are not measured here; pytest and the demo cover the mechanics. The model-dependence run on Mistral Large 4 was not made.

All sets were run on 16 November, after every prompt was restructured (static system prompts; text from users, memory and retrieved law passed as tagged data) and with the listwise rerank by the cheap model that replaced Cohere's Rerank 4 Fast on 3 November. The run of 27 October measured quick answers and full assessments with the Cohere ranking and the earlier prompts, so its numbers are not directly comparable with these.
The quick answers (E5) were run before the memory rule was reworded (see What follows); that rule is part of the quick-answer prompt too, and E5 was not repeated.
The judge's agreement with a human reader was measured on the run of 27 October only.
next: One change was made in response to a run. After the prompts were restructured, the first assessment run of 16 November (E6_20261116-1402) turned an internal rule from the organisation's memory, that the DPO reviews such assessments before build, into a finding of its own with a legal citation in four cases. The memory rule in the prompt was reworded and the set run again; the numbers reported here are the second run. Nothing else was changed in response to these numbers.

The right severity is the main gap: a short severity-calibration passage in the worker prompt, one example per severity written from the rubric's definitions rather than from these cases, tested on a fresh set; and a check in the output schema that the verdict follows from the severities of the findings.
Corpus side: the chunking of AI Act Art. 5.
Round 3 with the human expert: the unsure rows, the two disagreements, and the contested expectations (A-007, A-009 DPIA; A-012, A-017 Art. 9; A-010 Art. 22 on an automated hold).
intro: Seven sets, each testing one part of the assistant on its own test data, run once on the models the app ships with. Three sets test the guardrails around the models, two the retrieval of the law, two the whole path from a request to the answer.
data_note: The test data is synthetic: written with an AI assistant in the voice of a product manager, checked by the author, who is not a compliance professional, and reviewed in two rounds by a second AI model acting as the domain expert. A human expert's review is pending, so the expected answers are a careful draft, not a certified reference.
shortfalls_intro: Two of the nine targets were not met, both in the full assessments: verdict accuracy (15 of 20 against 0.80) and key findings matched (55 of 81 against 0.75). Two DPIA flags were also missed, and one case raised the DPIA and high-risk AI flags without cause. The failure modes below explain them; the first one accounts for most of the gap.
